says: In our tooling, the Reflect ban's fold (slice 15, ticket 1056) made law L4 miss the same fault three times in a row. Each time, one glob added to the JSON.parse warn block in .oxlintrc.json stripped client/'s Effect.retry and Stream.retry entries, or turned JSON.parse into advice where it blocks, with every law green. The cause: an override replaces a rule's options and a file takes the last override that matches it. Before the fold the Reflect list blocks came last and also recorded which folders block, so the old L4 could check one against the other. The fold put the entries in the base blocks, which keep main's order (next/**/*, then client/**, then the warn block last), so the warn block wins for any file its globs reach, client/ included. Then each version of L4 modeled oxlint's matching itself instead of asking oxlint about the real files: by block (miss 1), by folder at a coarser grain than the glob (miss 2), by one made-up file name per folder (miss 3).
proof: Reviews field/runs/2026-11-18-reflect-ban-s13-s15-review1.json, -review2.json and -review3.json: the globs next/packages/libfabrika/**, next/apps/fabrika/e2e/** and next/packages/libfabrika/src/**/*.test.ts each passed L4 while oxlint's real result for a client/ or access/ file changed. Plan docs/plan/quests/reflect-ban-PLAN.md, amendment 9.
cost: A fold that lets one glob silently loosen client/'s P18 rule or the JSON.parse guard. The fold's own pull request puts client/** back after the warn block and plants L4's sample at every tracked next/ file.
